drivingQuestion: Were the daily prayers instituted by the Patriarchs or established to correspond to the daily offerings, and how do the prayer deadlines follow?
outcomeNote: R' Yosei b. R' Ḥanina survives the attempted refutation: the Patriarchs instituted the prayers and the sages anchored them to the offerings. The havdala contradiction at 26b.3 is left as קשיא, and the pelag-haminḥa dilemma is answered from a baraita (last minḥa, eleven hours less a quarter).

segments.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: טָעָה וְלֹא הִתְפַּלֵּל מִנְחָה בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת — מִתְפַּלֵּל בְּלֵיל שַׁבָּת שְׁתַּיִם. טָעָה וְלֹא הִתְפַּלֵּל מִנְחָה בְּשַׁבָּת — מִתְפַּלֵּל בְּמוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת שְׁתַּיִם שֶׁל חוֹל. מַבְדִּיל בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה, וְאֵינוֹ מַבְדִּיל בִּשְׁנִיָּה. וְאִם הִבְדִּיל בַּשְּׁנִיָּה וְלֹא הִבְדִּיל בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה — שְׁנִיָּה עָלְתָה לוֹ, רִאשׁוֹנָה לֹא עָלְתָה לוֹ.
segments.en: On a similar note, «the Sages taught» in a baraita: «One who erred and did not recite the afternoon prayer on the eve of Shabbat, prays in» the evening prayer «two» Amida prayers «on Shabbat evening. One who erred and did not recite the afternoon prayer on Shabbat, recites two weekday» Amida prayers in the evening prayer «at the conclusion of Shabbat. He recites havdala [»the prayer of «distinction]» between the sanctity of Shabbat and the profanity of the week by reciting: You have graced us, etc., in the fourth blessing of the Amida, which is: Who graciously grants knowledge, «in the first» prayer, as it is the actual evening prayer, «but he does not recite havdala in the second» prayer, which is in place of the afternoon prayer. Moreover, «if he recited havdala in the second» prayer «and did not recite havdala in the first, the second prayer fulfilled his» obligation, the «first one did not fulfill his» obligation.

segments.he: לְמֵימְרָא דְּכֵיוָן דְּלָא אַבְדִּיל בְּקַמַּיְיתָא כְּמַאן דְּלָא צַלִּי דָּמֵי, וּמַהְדְּרִינַן לֵיהּ?
segments.en: The Gemara comments: «Is that to say» that «since he did not recite havdala in the first» prayer, he is «as one who did not pray and we require him to return» to the beginning of the prayer and repeat it? If so, the conclusion is that one who fails to recite havdala in the prayer must repeat that prayer.

segments.he: וּרְמִינְהוּ: טָעָה וְלֹא הִזְכִּיר גְּבוּרוֹת גְּשָׁמִים בִּתְחִיַּית הַמֵּתִים וּשְׁאֵלָה בְּבִרְכַּת הַשָּׁנִים — מַחֲזִירִין אוֹתוֹ. הַבְדָּלָה בְּ״חוֹנֵן הַדַּעַת״ אֵין מַחֲזִירִין אוֹתוֹ, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁיָּכוֹל לְאוֹמְרָהּ עַל הַכּוֹס! קַשְׁיָא.
segments.en: The Gemara «raises a contradiction» to the above conclusion from the Tosefta: «One who erred and did not mention the might of the rains:» He makes the wind blow and rain fall «in» the second blessing of the Amida, the blessing on «the revival of the dead, and» one who erred and failed to recite «the request» for rain «in» the ninth blessing of the Amida, «the blessing of the years, we require him to return» to the beginning of the prayer and repeat it. However, one who erred and failed to recite «havdala in» the blessing: «Who graciously grants knowledge, we do not require him to return» to the beginning of the prayer and repeat it, «as he can recite» havdala «over the cup» of wine, independent of his prayer. This contradiction was not resolved and remains «difficult.»

segments.he: אִיתְּמַר, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר: תְּפִלּוֹת אָבוֹת תִּקְּנוּם. רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמַר: תְּפִלּוֹת כְּנֶגֶד תְּמִידִין תִּקְּנוּם.
segments.en: The dispute between the Rabbis and Rabbi Yehuda with regard to the times beyond which the different prayers may not be recited is rooted in a profound disagreement, also manifest in a later amoraic dispute. «It was stated: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, said:» The practice of praying three times daily is ancient, albeit not in its present form; «prayers were instituted by the Patriarchs.» However, «Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said» that the «prayers were instituted based on the daily offerings» sacrificed in the Holy Temple, and the prayers parallel the offerings, in terms of both time and characteristics.

segments.he: תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא, וְתַנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי. תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: אַבְרָהָם תִּקֵּן תְּפִלַּת שַׁחֲרִית, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיַּשְׁכֵּם אַבְרָהָם בַּבֹּקֶר אֶל הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר עָמַד שָׁם״, וְאֵין ״עֲמִידָה״ אֶלָּא תְּפִלָּה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיַּעֲמֹד פִּינְחָס וַיְפַלֵּל״.
segments.en: The Gemara comments: «It was taught» in a baraita «in accordance with» the opinion of «Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, and it was taught» in a baraita «in accordance with» the opinion of «Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi.» The Gemara elaborates: «It was taught» in a baraita «in accordance with» the opinion of «Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina: Abraham instituted the morning prayer, as it is stated» when Abraham came to look out over Sodom the day after he had prayed on its behalf: «“And Abraham rose early in the morning to the place where he had stood» before the Lord” (Genesis 19:27), «and» from the context as well as the language utilized in the verse, the verb «standing» means «nothing other than prayer,» as this language is used to describe Pinehas’ prayer after the plague, «as it is stated: “And Pinehas stood up and prayed» and the plague ended” (Psalms 106:30). Clearly, Abraham was accustomed to stand in prayer in the morning.

segments.he: יִצְחָק תִּקֵּן תְּפִלַּת מִנְחָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וַיֵּצֵא יִצְחָק לָשׂוּחַ בַּשָּׂדֶה לִפְנוֹת עָרֶב״, וְאֵין ״שִׂיחָה״ אֶלָּא תְּפִלָּה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״תְּפִלָּה לְעָנִי כִי יַעֲטֹף וְלִפְנֵי ה׳ יִשְׁפֹּךְ שִׂיחוֹ״.
segments.en: «Isaac instituted the afternoon prayer, as it is stated: “And Isaac went out to converse [lasuaḥ] in the field toward evening”» (Genesis 24:63), «and conversation» means «nothing other than prayer, as it is stated: “A prayer of the afflicted when he is faint and pours out his complaint [siḥo] before the Lord”» (Psalms 102:1). Obviously, Isaac was the first to pray as evening approached, at the time of the afternoon prayer.

segments.he: יַעֲקֹב תִּקֵּן תְּפִלַּת עַרְבִית, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיִּפְגַּע בַּמָּקוֹם וַיָּלֶן שָׁם״, וְאֵין ״פְּגִיעָה״ אֶלָּא תְּפִלָּה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְאַתָּה אַל תִּתְפַּלֵּל בְּעַד הָעָם הַזֶּה וְאַל תִּשָּׂא בַעֲדָם רִנָּה וּתְפִלָּה וְאַל תִּפְגַּע בִּי״
segments.en: «Jacob instituted the evening prayer, as it is stated: “And he encountered [vayifga] the place and he slept there» for the sun had set” (Genesis 28:11). The word «encounter» means «nothing other than prayer, as it is stated» when God spoke to Jeremiah: «“And you, do not pray on behalf of this nation and do not raise on their behalf song and prayer, and do not encounter [tifga] Me» for I do not hear you” (Jeremiah 7:16). Jacob prayed during the evening, after the sun had set.

segments.he: וְתַנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: מִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרוּ תְּפִלַּת הַשַּׁחַר עַד חֲצוֹת — שֶׁהֲרֵי תָּמִיד שֶׁל שַׁחַר קָרֵב וְהוֹלֵךְ עַד חֲצוֹת. וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד אַרְבַּע שָׁעוֹת שֶׁהֲרֵי תָּמִיד שֶׁל שַׁחַר קָרֵב וְהוֹלֵךְ עַד אַרְבַּע שָׁעוֹת.
segments.en: «And it was taught» in a baraita «in accordance with» the opinion of «Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi» that the laws of prayer are based on the laws of the daily offerings: «Why did» the Rabbis «say» that «the morning prayer» may be recited «until noon? Because,» although the «daily morning offering» is typically brought early in the morning, it may be «sacrificed until noon. And Rabbi Yehuda says:» My opinion, that the morning prayer may be recited «until four hours» into the day, is «because the daily morning offering is sacrificed until four hours.»

segments.he: וּמִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרוּ תְּפִלַּת הַמִּנְחָה עַד הָעֶרֶב — שֶׁהֲרֵי, תָּמִיד שֶׁל בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם קָרֵב וְהוֹלֵךְ עַד הָעֶרֶב. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד פְּלַג הַמִּנְחָה, שֶׁהֲרֵי תָּמִיד שֶׁל בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם קָרֵב וְהוֹלֵךְ עַד פְּלַג הַמִּנְחָה.
segments.en: «And why did» the Rabbis «say» that «the afternoon prayer» may be recited «until the evening? Because the daily afternoon offering is sacrificed until the evening. Rabbi Yehuda says» that «the afternoon prayer» may be recited only «until the midpoint of the afternoon because,» according to his opinion, «the daily afternoon offering is sacrificed until the midpoint of the afternoon.»

segments.he: וּמִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרוּ תְּפִלַּת הָעֶרֶב אֵין לָהּ קֶבַע — שֶׁהֲרֵי אֵבָרִים וּפְדָרִים שֶׁלֹּא נִתְעַכְּלוּ מִבָּעֶרֶב, קְרֵבִים וְהוֹלְכִים כׇּל הַלַּיְלָה.
segments.en: «And why did they say» that «the evening prayer is not fixed? Because» the burning of the «limbs and fats» of the offerings that were «not consumed» by the fire on the altar «until the evening.» They remained on the altar and were «offered continuously» throughout «the entire night.»

segments.he: וּמִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרוּ שֶׁל מוּסָפִין כׇּל הַיּוֹם — שֶׁהֲרֵי קׇרְבָּן שֶׁל מוּסָפִין קָרֵב כׇּל הַיּוֹם. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד שֶׁבַע שָׁעוֹת, שֶׁהֲרֵי קׇרְבַּן מוּסַף קָרֵב וְהוֹלֵךְ עַד שֶׁבַע שָׁעוֹת.
segments.en: «And why did» the Rabbis «say» that «the additional prayer» may be recited «all day? Because the additional offering is brought» throughout «the entire day.» However, «Rabbi Yehuda says» that «the additional prayer» may be recited «until the seventh hour» of the day, «because the additional offering is sacrificed until the seventh hour.»

segments.he: וְאֵיזוֹ הִיא מִנְחָה גְדוֹלָה מִשֵּׁשׁ שָׁעוֹת וּמֶחֱצָה וּלְמַעְלָה. וְאֵיזוֹ הִיא מִנְחָה קְטַנָּה מִתֵּשַׁע שָׁעוֹת וּמֶחֱצָה וּלְמַעְלָה.
segments.en: The baraita continues and states that there are two times for the afternoon prayer. Greater, earlier minḥa [minḥa gedola] and lesser, later minḥa [minḥa ketana]. The Gemara clarifies the difference between them: «Which is minḥa gedola? From six-and-a-half hours» after sunrise «and on,» which is a half an hour after noon and on. It is the earliest time that the daily afternoon offering may be sacrificed, as in the case on the eve of Passover that occurs on Shabbat. «Which is minḥa ketana? From nine-and-a-half hours and on,» which is the standard time that the daily afternoon offering is sacrificed.

segments.he: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, פְּלַג מִנְחָה קַמָּא קָאָמַר אוֹ פְּלַג מִנְחָה אַחֲרוֹנָה קָאָמַר? תָּא שְׁמַע דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: פְּלַג הַמִּנְחָה אַחֲרוֹנָה אָמְרוּ, וְהִיא אַחַת עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁעוֹת חָסֵר רְבִיעַ.
segments.en: On that note, «a dilemma was raised before them: Rabbi Yehuda,» who holds that the afternoon prayer may be recited only until the midpoint of the afternoon, does «he say the midpoint of the first minḥa,» minḥa gedola? «Or,» does «he say the midpoint of the last minḥa? Come and hear» an explicit resolution to this dilemma: «As it was taught» in a baraita, «Rabbi Yehuda says: They said the midpoint of the last minḥa, and that is eleven hours minus a quarter» of an hour after sunrise, i.e., an hour-and-a-quarter hours before sunset.

segments.he: נֵימָא תֶּיהְוֵי תְּיוּבְתֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא? אָמַר לְךָ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: לְעוֹלָם אֵימָא לָךְ, תְּפִלּוֹת, אָבוֹת תִּקְּנוּם, וְאַסְמְכִינְהוּ רַבָּנַן אַקׇּרְבָּנוֹת. דְּאִי לָא תֵּימָא הָכִי, תְּפִלַּת מוּסָף לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא מַאן תַּקְּנַהּ. אֶלָּא תְּפִלּוֹת אָבוֹת תִּקְּנוּם, וְאַסְמְכִינְהוּ רַבָּנַן אַקׇּרְבָּנוֹת.
segments.en: In any case, it is clear that according to this baraita the halakhot of prayer are based on the Temple offerings. The Gemara suggests: «Let us say that this is a conclusive refutation of» the opinion of «Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina,» who held that the forefathers instituted the prayers. «Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina,» could have «said to you: Actually, I will say to you» that «the Patriarchs instituted the prayers and the Sages based» the times and characteristics of prayer «on the Temple offerings,» even though they do not stem from the same source. «As, if you do not say so,» that even Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, would agree that the laws of offerings and those of prayers are related, «then, according to Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, who instituted the additional prayer?» It is not one of the prayers instituted by the forefathers. «Rather,» even according to Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, «the prayers were instituted by the Patriarchs and the Sages based them» on the laws of the «offerings.»

moves.summary: baraita: missed minḥa on Shabbat eve or Shabbat is made up at evening; havdala in the first prayer only
moves.about: one who missed minḥa on Shabbat eve or on Shabbat prays twice at the evening prayer; havdala goes in the first prayer

moves.summary: infers that one who omitted havdala is as if he had not prayed and must repeat
moves.about: from 'the first did not count' it follows that one who omitted havdala in prayer is as if he did not pray and must repeat

moves.summary: Tosefta: omitted havdala does not send one back, since it can be said over the cup
moves.about: the baraita implies omitted havdala forces repetition, while the Tosefta says one who omitted havdala is not sent back since he can say it over the cup

moves.summary: the contradiction is left standing
moves.about: omitted rain-mention or rain-request sends one back; omitted havdala does not

moves.summary: the prayers were instituted by the Patriarchs
moves.about: who instituted the daily prayers — the Patriarchs, or the sages modelling them on the daily offerings

moves.summary: the prayers were instituted corresponding to the daily offerings
moves.about: the prayers were instituted by the Patriarchs

moves.cueHe: תניא כוותיה דרבי יוסי ברבי חנינא
moves.summary: announces baraitot for each view; the first: Abraham instituted the morning prayer ('standing' is prayer)
moves.about: the baraita on the Patriarchs instituting the three prayers

moves.summary: the baraita continues: Isaac instituted the afternoon prayer ('conversing' is prayer)
moves.about: Isaac went out to converse in the field toward evening

moves.summary: the baraita continues: Jacob instituted the evening prayer ('encountering' is prayer)
moves.about: Jacob encountered the place and slept there

moves.cueHe: ותניא כוותיה דרבי יהושע בן לוי
moves.summary: baraita: the morning prayer is until noon because the morning tamid is offered until noon
moves.about: the baraita grounding each prayer's deadline in the time of its offering

moves.cueHe: ורבי יהודה אומר: עד ארבע שעות
moves.summary: until four hours, because the morning tamid is offered until four hours
moves.about: the latest time for the morning, afternoon and additional prayers — until noon / evening / all day, or four hours / pelag haminḥa / seven hours — each tied to when its offering is brought

moves.cueHe: ומפני מה אמרו תפלת המנחה עד הערב
moves.summary: minḥa until evening because the afternoon tamid is offered until evening

moves.cueHe: רבי יהודה אומר: עד פלג המנחה
moves.summary: until pelag haminḥa, because on his view the afternoon tamid is offered until then

moves.cueHe: ומפני מה אמרו תפלת הערב אין לה קבע
moves.summary: the evening prayer has no fixed time because limbs and fats burn all night

moves.cueHe: ומפני מה אמרו של מוספין כל היום
moves.summary: musaf all day because the musaf offering is brought all day

moves.cueHe: רבי יהודה אומר: עד שבע שעות
moves.summary: until seven hours, because the musaf offering is brought until seven hours
defines minḥa gedola (from six and a half hours) and minḥa ketana (from nine and a half hours)
moves.about: defines the baraita's minḥa gedola (from six and a half hours) and minḥa ketana (from nine and a half hours)

moves.cueHe: איבעיא להו: רבי יהודה, פלג מנחה קמא קאמר
moves.summary: does R' Yehuda's pelag haminḥa mean the midpoint of the first minḥa or of the last?
moves.about: whether R' Yehuda's 'pelag haminḥa' means the midpoint of the first minḥa or of the last

moves.summary: baraita: R' Yehuda says the midpoint of the last minḥa, eleven hours less a quarter — accepted as an explicit resolution
moves.about: R' Yehuda: they said the midpoint of the last minḥa, eleven hours less a quarter

moves.cueHe: נימא תיהוי תיובתיה דרבי יוסי ברבי חנינא
moves.summary: shall we say the offerings baraita refutes R' Yosei b. R' Ḥanina?
moves.about: the baraita anchoring prayer times in the offerings refutes the view that the Patriarchs instituted the prayers

moves.cueHe: אמר לך רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא: לעולם אימא לך
moves.summary: on his behalf: the Patriarchs instituted the prayers and the sages anchored them to the offerings
moves.about: the Patriarchs instituted the prayers and the sages then based their times on the offerings

moves.summary: otherwise, who on his view instituted musaf? so the sages must have linked prayers to offerings
moves.about: even on his view the sages must have linked prayers to offerings, since no Patriarch instituted musaf

moves.summary: rather: the Patriarchs instituted them and the sages anchored them to the offerings

edges.about: one who missed minḥa on Shabbat eve or on Shabbat prays twice at the evening prayer; havdala goes in the first prayer
from 'the first did not count' it follows that one who omitted havdala in prayer is as if he did not pray and must repeat
the baraita implies omitted havdala forces repetition, while the Tosefta says one who omitted havdala is not sent back since he can say it over the cup
omitted rain-mention or rain-request sends one back; omitted havdala does not
the contradiction over repeating a prayer that lacked havdala is left standing

edges.cueHe: איתמר, רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא אמר
edges.about: the prayers were instituted by the Patriarchs
the prayers were instituted corresponding to the daily offerings

edges.cueHe: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא אמר ... רבי יהושע בן לוי אמר
edges.about: who instituted the daily prayers — the Patriarchs, or the sages modelling them on the daily offerings

edges.cueHe: תניא כוותיה דרבי יוסי ברבי חנינא
edges.about: a baraita deriving each prayer from a Patriarch supports 'the Patriarchs instituted the prayers'

edges.cueHe: ותניא כוותיה דרבי יהושע בן לוי
edges.about: a baraita tying each prayer's deadline to its offering supports 'the prayers correspond to the daily offerings'
the baraita on the Patriarchs instituting the three prayers
Abraham rose early to the place where he had stood
'Pinehas stood up and prayed' — standing means prayer
Abraham's 'standing' in the morning is prayer, so he instituted the morning prayer
Isaac went out to converse in the field toward evening
'pours out his complaint before the Lord' — conversing means prayer
Isaac's 'conversing' toward evening is prayer, so he instituted the afternoon prayer
Jacob encountered the place and slept there
'do not encounter Me' — encountering means prayer
Jacob's 'encountering' the place at nightfall is prayer, so he instituted the evening prayer
the baraita grounding each prayer's deadline in the time of its offering

edges.cueHe: מפני מה אמרו ... ורבי יהודה אומר
edges.about: the latest time for the morning, afternoon and additional prayers — until noon / evening / all day, or four hours / pelag haminḥa / seven hours — each tied to when its offering is brought
defines the baraita's minḥa gedola (from six and a half hours) and minḥa ketana (from nine and a half hours)
whether R' Yehuda's 'pelag haminḥa' means the midpoint of the first minḥa or of the last

edges.about: which minḥa R' Yehuda's 'pelag haminḥa' refers to
R' Yehuda: they said the midpoint of the last minḥa, eleven hours less a quarter
the baraita in which R' Yehuda specifies the last minḥa resolves the dilemma
